episodes.title: Start here: how to read a Polaris model name

segments.t: Welcome to Torque product training. In this first episode: how to read a model name, what the trims mean, and the three numbers customers ask about most.
Decoding a model name
A full model name contains several separate identifiers.
Example: RANGER CREW XP 1000 NorthStar Ultimate identifies family, passenger configuration, platform, cab/trim, and equipment tier.
Model codes identify exact catalog rows; a stock number identifies a dealer unit.
A model number is not a complete specification and does not always equal engine displacement.
Remember it like this: Year → family → platform → seats → trim → finish.
E P S, cab and NorthStar
Abbreviations describe equipment, but their availability depends on the model and year.
E P S means electronic power steering.
Cab identifies an enclosure configuration; it alone does not establish air conditioning.
The 2026 RANGER XP 1000 NorthStar Premium table explicitly includes heating and air conditioning.
Remember it like this: E P S = electronic power steering.
Towing, payload and the cargo box
Towing capacity, vehicle payload, and cargo-box capacity describe different limits.
Towing capacity concerns the trailer being pulled.
Payload concerns weight carried by the vehicle, subject to the manual’s definition.
A cargo-box limit is a separate limit for the box; it is not the entire vehicle payload.
Remember it like this: Three separate weight limits.
Reading a spec sheet
A specification is meaningful only with its units and configuration.
Displacement in cc is different from horsepower.
Ground clearance is different from suspension travel.
MSRP is different from a dealer advertised price; both are dated references.
Remember it like this: Rating + units + exact model year.
Identifying a unit on the lot
Use a consistent identification sequence for every machine.
Read the full model year and name.
Identify the platform and trim before memorizing specifications.
Use the stock number to distinguish individual units with the same model name.
Remember it like this: Year → family → model → trim → equipment.
This episode is the RANGER family: what it's for, every model smallest to biggest, the comparisons customers make, and a quick quiz.
What RANGER is for
RANGER is the utility side-by-side family, with distinct size, drivetrain, and cab branches.
1000, XP 1000, XD 1500, and XP Kinetic are separate model lines.
CREW identifies a longer passenger configuration; seat count depends on the platform.
The 2026 book uses SP 570 in the mid-size range; the model year 2027 sheet lists RANGER 600.
Remember it like this: RANGER = utility side-by-side.
The lineup, smallest to biggest

The RANGER 500. 28 horsepower from a 567 C C engine. It seats 2, tows 1,500 pounds, carries 500 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,000 pounds. It's 58.5 inches wide and 110 inches long, with 10 inches of ground clearance. It has no power steering. The tank holds 9.5 gallons of gas. Warranty: 1-year limited.

The RANGER 600. 44 horsepower from a 567 C C engine. It seats 2, tows 1,500 pounds, carries 500 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,000 pounds. It's 56 inches wide and 108 inches long, with 15 inches of ground clearance. It has no power steering. The tank holds 13.6 gallons of gas. Warranty: 1-year limited.
The RANGER SP 570. 44 horsepower from a 567 C C engine. It tows 1,500 pounds and carries 500 pounds in the box. It has 11 inches of ground clearance. The tank holds 9.5 gallons of gas.

The RANGER 1000. 61 horsepower from a 999 C C engine. It seats 3, tows 2,500 pounds, carries 1,000 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,500 pounds. It's 62.5 inches wide and 120 inches long, with 12 inches of ground clearance. It has no power steering. The tank holds 11.35 gallons of gas. Warranty: 1-year limited.

The RANGER XP 1000. 82 horsepower from a 999 C C engine. It seats 6, tows 2,500 pounds, carries 1,000 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,125 pounds. It's 65 inches wide and 152 inches long, with 14 inches of ground clearance. It has power steering. The tank holds 11.5 gallons of gas. Warranty: 1-year limited.

The RANGER XP 1000 Premium. 82 horsepower from a 999 C C engine. It seats 3, carries 1,000 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,500 pounds. It's 62.5 inches wide and 120 inches long, with 14 inches of ground clearance. It has power steering. The tank holds 11.5 gallons of gas.

The RANGER Crew XD 1500. 110 horsepower from a 1,498 C C engine. It seats 6, tows 3,500 pounds, carries 1,300 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,420 pounds. It's 65 inches wide and 164 inches long, with 16 inches of ground clearance. It has no power steering and the sealed STEELDRIVE transmission. The tank holds 13.6 gallons of gas. Warranty: 2-year limited.

The RANGER XD 1500. 110 horsepower from a 1,498 C C engine. It tows 3,500 pounds, carries 1,500 pounds in the box and has a total payload of 1,650 pounds. It's 65 inches wide and 164 inches long, with 15 inches of ground clearance. It has power steering and the sealed STEELDRIVE transmission. The tank holds 13.6 gallons of gas. Warranty: 2-year limited.
The RANGER Crew 1000 Premium. It seats 6 and has a total payload of 1,700 pounds. It's 152 inches long, with 12.5 inches of ground clearance.
The RANGER Crew SP 570 Premium. It has a total payload of 1,200 pounds. It's 56 inches wide and 144 inches long. It has no power steering.
The RANGER SP 570 NorthStar Edition. It seats 2 and has a total payload of 675 pounds. It's 58 inches wide and 108 inches long. It has power steering.
Quick comparisons
Who makes the most power? The RANGER XP 1000, at 82 horsepower. Then the RANGER 1000 at 61, the RANGER 600 at 44 and the RANGER 500 at 28.
Who's narrowest for tight trails? The RANGER 150 E F I, at 48 inches. Then the RANGER 600 at 56, the RANGER 500 at 58.5 and the RANGER XD 1500 at 65.
Who's longest? The RANGER XP 1000, at 152 inches. Then the RANGER XD 1500 at 137, the RANGER 1000 at 120 and the RANGER 500 at 110.
Who has the most ground clearance? The RANGER XD 1500, at 16 inches. Then the RANGER XP 1000 at 14 and the RANGER SP 570 at 11.
Who has the biggest cargo box? The RANGER XD 1500, at 1,500 pounds. Then the RANGER 1000 at 1,000 and the RANGER 600 at 500.
Who carries the most payload? The RANGER XD 1500, at 1,675 pounds. Then the RANGER 1000 at 1,500 and the RANGER 150 E F I at 375.
Who holds the most gas? The RANGER 600, at 13.6 gallons. Then the RANGER XP 1000 at 11.5, the RANGER 1000 at 11.35 and the RANGER 150 E F I at 2.5.

episodes.title: Side-by-side showdown: which one for which customer

segments.t: Across all the side-by-sides: who tows the most, who's narrowest for tight trails, who carries the most. These are the questions that decide a sale.
Across the families
Who makes the most power? The RZR Pro XP 4, at 181 horsepower. Then the XPEDITION ADV at 114, the GENERAL 1000 at 100 and the RANGER 500 at 28.
Who's narrowest for tight trails? The GENERAL 1000, at 62.5 inches. Then the RZR Pro XP 4 at 64, the RANGER XP 1000 at 65 and the RZR XP S 1000 at 72.
Who's longest? The RANGER XD 1500, at 164 inches. Then the GENERAL XP 4 1000 at 150.2 and the RANGER 600 at 108.
Who has the most ground clearance? The RZR XP S 1000, at 16 inches. Then the RZR XP 4 1000 at 14, the GENERAL 1000 at 12 and the RANGER 500 at 10.
Who tows the most? The RANGER XD 1500, at 3,500 pounds. Then the RANGER XP 1000 at 2,500, the XPEDITION XP at 2,000 and the RANGER SP 570 at 1,500.
Who has the biggest cargo box? The RANGER XP 1000, at 1,000 pounds. Then the XPEDITION ADV at 600, the RANGER 500 at 500 and the RZR XP 4 1000 at 300.
Who carries the most payload? The RANGER XP 1000, at 1,500 pounds. Then the GENERAL XP 4 1000 at 1,100 and the XPEDITION XP at 1,000.
Who holds the most gas? The RZR Pro XP 4, at 13 gallons. Then the RZR Pro XP at 12, the GENERAL XP 1000 at 9.5 and the RANGER 150 E F I at 2.5.
Fifty-inch trails
If a customer rides fifty-inch trails, only the narrow machines fit. Anything sixty inches or wider won't. Ask where they ride before you show anything.
Quiz yourself
Question. Of these side-by-sides, which one has the most horsepower?
Answer: 2026 Polaris RZR PRO XP 4.
Pontoons and tritoons, and how to read a Bennington model name.
Pontoon versus tritoon
Pontoon boats use buoyant tubes under a deck; a tritoon configuration has three.
Tube count is distinct from boat length and floorplan.
Bennington is represented in the inventory.
Capacity, engine rating, installed motor, and tube package belong to the exact boat configuration.
Remember it like this: Two tubes or three; then the exact package.
Bennington model names
Bennington model names combine a series and a floorplan designation.
SX and R are different series labels.
Similar length designations can have different seating and floorplans.
The model name does not by itself identify every installed engine, tube package, or option.
Remember it like this: Series + length designation + floorplan.
Boat dimensions and capacity
Boat capacity and trailering dimensions are separate specifications.
Use the capacity plate and exact manufacturer information for load and people limits.
Loaded trailering weight includes the relevant boat, motor, trailer, fuel, and gear.
Storage dimensions include the trailer and fitted equipment, not just hull length.
Remember it like this: Length, capacity, and loaded weight differ.

FourStroke and Pro XS
Pro XS is a performance-oriented Mercury product line; four-stroke describes engine operation.
Pro XS engines can also be four-strokes.
Horsepower alone does not establish engine weight, controls, or gearcase.
Read the complete model and specification sheet.

Shaft length and rigging
Rigging includes the components that connect the engine with the boat’s controls and systems.
Shaft length must match the boat’s installation requirements.
Steering, controls, starting, and trim are separate configuration details.

Propeller and engine setup affect how the complete boat performs.

Read shaft length and control type.

Trailers and accessories: reading a trailer spec and making sure accessories fit.
Trailer specs
GVWR is the maximum rated total trailer weight, including the trailer itself.
Approximate payload is GVWR minus empty trailer weight, subject to all other applicable ratings.
Usable deck dimensions and ramp ratings are separate fields.
Axle, tire, coupler, hitch, and towing limits must also be respected.
Remember it like this: GVWR − empty weight = available payload.
Accessory fit
Accessory fit depends on the exact machine configuration.
An accessory for one model year may not fit another.
Included equipment is different from an optional accessory.
Mounting hardware and installation requirements are separate from the accessory’s name.
Remember it like this: Year + model + trim + installation.
